title: Denmark Faces Defining Trade-Off Between Security Spending and Household… · 19 Oct
keywords: Denmark, defence spending, fiscal policy, EU budget, cost of living, inflation, NATO, European Union, tax cuts, security policy, multiannual financial framework, household prices, overheating risk, European defence
notes: Denmark is navigating one of its most consequential fiscal moments in a generation, pushing defence expenditure toward 3.5 percent of GDP by 2030 while simultaneously proposing tax cuts that critics warn could overheat an already stretched economy. At the same time, Copenhagen is entering difficult negotiations over the EU's next long-term budget, covering 2028 to 2034, with Danish households still feeling the weight of elevated prices. The collision between strategic ambition and domestic cost-of-living politics is reshaping the country's political debate and offers a preview of pressures building across the European Union.
